content: Firebase auth docs (fetched 2026-08-06): deleteUser is a security-sensitive action requiring RECENT sign-in — otherwise auth/requires-recent-login; fix is reauthenticateWithCredential(user, EmailAuthProvider.credential(email,password)) which grants a fresh window. Pitfalls: reauth needs network (offline = cannot reauth); after reauth the window is short (minutes-scale, exact value not formally documented). Cascade order matters: deleting the auth user triggers onAuthStateChanged(null) immediately, unmounting the signed-in UI mid-cascade — so Firestore deletes must complete BEFORE deleteUser(). Firestore batch limit is 500 ops per batch (official docs) — account deletion needs chunking if >500 entries. Partial failure (e.g. network drop mid-cascade) leaves dangling Firestore docs with no auth user; design should delete Firestore data first, auth last, and tolerate retries.
